title: Women’s Health Initiative estrogen-plus-progestin trial: chronic-disease-prevention expectation reversed by randomized hard outcomes
summary: The estrogen-plus-progestin component of the Women’s Health Initiative is promoted as a medical negative-result/reversal record. The trial tested combined hormone therapy in healthy postmenopausal women, after decades of observational and intermediate-outcome support for potential cardioprotection. The data and safety board recommended stopping early because the invasive breast-cancer statistic crossed a stopping boundary and the global index supported risks exceeding benefits. The record is scoped to chronic-disease prevention with the studied oral regimen, not to all menopausal hormone therapy uses, ages, formulations, or symptom-relief contexts.

limitations: The record covers oral estrogen-plus-progestin primary prevention; it does not adjudicate all menopause symptom treatment.
Subsequent WHI follow-up, age/timing hypotheses, and formulation-specific debates require child records.

type_payload.hypothesis_or_claim_tested: Combined estrogen-plus-progestin therapy could provide a favorable chronic-disease-prevention risk/benefit profile, especially for coronary heart disease, in healthy postmenopausal women.
type_payload.hard_endpoint_result: Global hard clinical outcomes did not support primary-prevention use; the trial stopped early for an adverse breast-cancer boundary and overall risk-benefit imbalance.
positive_findings_preserved: fewer colorectal cancers in the 2002 global-index report
fewer hip fractures in the 2002 report
scope_cautions: Do not generalize to all menopausal hormone therapy, all ages, or all formulations/routes.
Symptom-relief indication is separate from chronic-disease prevention.
Current evidence and guidance may be formulation- and timing-sensitive.
type_payload.practice_lag_seed: The record needs later linkage to prescribing trends, FDA labels, professional guidelines, and patient communication after 2002.
